analysis.investment_thesis: FEDFINA is a Federal Bank-backed NBFC with impressive 32% revenue CAGR, but a declining FY25 net profit (₹245 Cr → ₹225 Cr) and anaemic ROE of 8.84% signal margin compression and poor capital efficiency that undermine the growth story. At Forward P/E of 11.35x the valuation is undemanding, but I need to see ROE consistently above 15% before taking a serious position.
key_strengths: Federal Bank parentage (60.79% promoter) provides funding access, governance credibility, and brand halo in a trust-sensitive lending business.
Strong 3-year revenue CAGR of 32.2% and loan book expansion from ₹6,556 Cr to ₹13,250 Cr in assets — clear proof of scale-up execution.
Reasonable valuation at 17.5x trailing P/E and 11.35x forward P/E with DII holding of 18.82% indicating institutional confidence.
key_risks: ROE of only 8.84% is well below my 15% floor — the FY24 equity infusion (IPO proceeds pushed equity from ₹1,356 Cr to ₹2,261 Cr) has diluted returns and recovery timeline is unclear.
FY25 net profit actually fell 8% (₹245 Cr → ₹225 Cr) and EBITDA compressed (₹415 Cr → ₹385 Cr) despite 30% revenue growth — rising credit costs or funding costs are squeezing spreads dangerously.
Intensely competitive NBFC landscape (gold loans: Muthoot/Manappuram; LAP/home loans: HDFC/LIC HF) with no pricing power moat; FEDFINA is a subscale player in every segment it competes in.
red_flags: Profit declined in FY25 despite 32% revenue growth — a spread compression signal that must be watched closely in a rising credit-cost environment.
Negative operating cash flow all 4 years (normal for NBFCs but FCF of -₹996 Cr in FY25 means total dependence on debt markets; any liquidity squeeze would be brutal at D/E of 3.83x).
analysis.detailed_analysis:
FEDFINA has the hallmarks of a solid franchise in the making — Federal Bank parentage, diversified loan products, and a strong 3-year growth CAGR of 32%. The promoter holding at 60.79% is stable, governance risk is low, and the company has genuinely expanded its balance sheet from ₹6,556 Cr to ₹13,250 Cr over three years. The Forward P/E of 11.35x reflects market skepticism, which creates an entry opportunity — but only if fundamentals improve.

The problem is the FY25 numbers tell a worrying story. Revenue grew 30% to ₹1,973 Cr, yet net profit *fell* 8% to ₹225 Cr. That means spreads are compressing — either cost of funds is rising faster than yields, or credit costs (loan losses) are climbing. ROE of 8.84% is simply too low for a lending business; I want to see 15%+ before I deploy meaningful capital. FEDFINA is not a bad company, but it is an average NBFC in a brutally competitive space, and the current margin trend is going the wrong way. I'd watch two more quarters for evidence of spread stabilization before reconsidering.
